pieces.name: Document model & block identity
pieces.scope: ProseMirror schema shaped like OOXML; stable anchors that ride transactions
pieces.evidence: 5/5 identity tests pass: typing preserves anchors, split keeps identity on the first half, paste de-duplicates, delete is clean
pieces.gap: Not yet exercised against a real .docx-derived document.

pieces.name: App shell & host seam
pieces.scope: React chrome, ProseMirror surface, bun server implementing HostApi
pieces.evidence: The app runs. Real .md opened from disk, edited and saved back correctly — frontmatter, GFM table, ordered list, bold, em-dash, CJK and ± all survived. Live status bar reads 2.7 ms p99 keystroke latency in a real browser, including ProseMirror’s DOM write, against an 8 ms budget.
pieces.gap: Only the Markdown path is wired. Opening a .docx in the app is not possible yet, so the document-polish comparison against Google Docs cannot be run.

pieces.name: Markdown ⇄ model
pieces.evidence: 96.19% idempotent across 1,442 real corpus files (README/docs from major open-source repos), zero parse or serialize errors. 36 tests, 282k assertions.
pieces.gap: The 3.8% that fails is concentrated in nested-list indentation, blockquote nesting and repeated-asterisk emphasis — all real, all characterized.

pieces.name: docx import, sidecar & anchors
pieces.scope: Offset-recording XML index, fidelity sidecar, alignment-based re-anchoring
pieces.evidence: 288/288 real Word documents import without throwing. Mean text recovery 99.49%; 260/286 files recover ≥99.5% of every <w:t> in the source. The fidelity ledger is populated and honest: 791 degraded entries, 144 informational.
pieces.gap: Text inside text boxes and content controls is dropped — the worst file recovers only 64.5%. The ledger names it (327 inline-drawing-detached, 75 content-control-unwrapped) rather than hiding it.

pieces.name: Round-trip scorer & corpus
pieces.scope: Real-world .docx corpus, three-tier fidelity score, pandoc baseline
pieces.evidence: Corpus collected and validated: 288/288 valid .docx — 235 with numbering, 121 headers/footers, ~33% tables, 12 comments.
pieces.gap: No fidelity tier can run until the export splice engine exists.

pieces.name: Latency gate
pieces.scope: Keystroke budget enforced by a test that fails the build
pieces.evidence: Gate runs and fails the build correctly (exit 1). Keystroke → state commit on a 40,040-word document: p99 0.38ms against an 8ms budget, n=15,000, typed from real Gutenberg prose.
pieces.gap: Keystroke → paint is still unmeasured, so the 16ms end-to-end budget is unproven. The state-commit figure is reported as a lower bound, not a pass.

pieces.name: Smart text ops
pieces.scope: Selection-aware surrounds, multi-cursor, motions, transpose, join, kill-line
pieces.gap: Only locale data and text helpers landed; no commands yet.

pieces.name: Prose IntelliSense
pieces.scope: Workspace symbol index, completions, Harper diagnostics over an LSP seam

pieces.name: AI inline edit
pieces.scope: Cmd-K streaming rewrite as accept/reject diff; three-way merge; agent mode

pieces.name: Workspace & git
pieces.scope: Fuzzy open, search, diff and blame at sentence granularity
pieces.evidence: Sentence segmentation, alignment and word-level intra-sentence diff landed.
pieces.gap: File tree, fuzzy open and search not started; nothing measured.

pieces.name: docx export splice
pieces.scope: Edit the original zip rather than regenerate it

decisions.d: ProseMirror, used directly — not Tiptap, not Lexical
decisions.why: Pure decorations are load-bearing for AI diffs, diagnostics and blame. Lexical and Quill lack them; Tiptap's auto-schema fights the OOXML mapping.

decisions.d: Splice the original zip; never regenerate it
decisions.why: Turns 'how much OOXML can we model?' into 'how little must we touch?'. An unedited round-trip is byte-identical, and fidelity degrades only in proportion to what was actually edited.

decisions.d: Exact in-session, fuzzy only for externally-edited files
decisions.why: While the doc is open we observed every change, so identity needs no guessing. Sequence alignment is reserved for files edited by another tool — that split is what makes the problem tractable.

decisions.d: Drop formatting rather than risk misapplying it
decisions.why: A dropped style is a visible bug the writer can fix; a misapplied one silently corrupts a document they trusted.

decisions.d: harper.js in a worker, behind an LSP-shaped seam
decisions.why: Offline, Apache-2.0, works unchanged in web v1 and Tauri v2. The LSP shape makes adding a second checker cheap.

decisions.d: A measurement that covers only part of a path may fail a budget but may never certify a pass
decisions.why: A headless process cannot see the DOM half of a keystroke. Reporting it as 'pass' would manufacture confidence in a number that never measured the thing it names.

notes: The gate is currently RED, deliberately and correctly: importing large Word documents takes p99 3.35s against a 1.2s budget. A 84ms average across the whole corpus had hidden this — the large documents are the bottleneck.

A status-bar reading that looked like two bugs turned out to be the 220 ms coalescing timer doing its job — the status store deliberately keeps typing off React’s render path. Verified by measurement rather than patched on suspicion.
Both session interruptions cost roughly a wave each. Builders now commit after every deliverable, which is why nothing was lost the second time.
The .docx corpus is public real-world documents. The 59 .docx files in ~/Downloads are personal and are deliberately not used.
